name: Sybil Rey
life: Sybil was once praised for spotting a small overpayment while the service was losing a fortune in mileage. She has never forgotten what the praise taught her about which details rise through an office. People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Sybil by a small Wednesday habit. Sybil usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: The second portion costs less than my mileage for investigating it. I can't erase the charge, but I can put both numbers on the same sheet for the person reviewing it.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a boxy denim jacket and a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. Sybil has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Sybil folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Sybil is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Sybil is concerned.
agenda: To show both the food cost and the investigation cost on the review.
family: Elsa Allen is Sybil’s cousin. Sybil asks before bringing somebody along. Elsa can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Midnight cinnamon*, Elsa says, “I was fasting when the first tray came out.”
connections: Amin Bach. The cost of a twist of pepper is the auditor's smallest example of the difference between meals and people.

reactions.response: Sybil asks for a meal to be held while the people who eat it explain the second portion.
